title: Same Budget, Same Payoff Date - Why the Order Still Costs You Money
description:
Two popular ways to pay off multiple debts faster: snowball (smallest balance first) or avalanche (highest rate first). We run both against the same three credit cards and the same $400 monthly budget - they finish in the exact same month, but the total interest isn't the same.

This video uses AI-generated narration and visuals.

#Shorts #debtpayoff #creditcarddebt #personalfinance

segments.text: Three credit cards. Four hundred dollars a month, same as always. Pay them off with the wrong strategy and it quietly costs you real money.
There are two popular ways to order the extra payment: snowball, smallest balance first, or avalanche, highest interest rate first.
Card A: five hundred dollars at twenty-two percent. Card B: two thousand at eighteen percent. Card C: six thousand at twenty-four percent.
Run both strategies with the exact same four hundred dollar monthly budget, and they finish on the exact same month: twenty-eight months, just under two and a half years.
But the interest bill isn't the same. Snowball costs twenty-five hundred seventy-two dollars. Avalanche costs twenty-three hundred thirty-nine.

slide.headline: Total interest paid - same budget, same payoff date

segments.text: Same monthly payment. Same finish line. Avalanche just saves you two hundred thirty-three dollars, for making one different choice each month: which card gets the extra.
Speed feels identical either way. The order is what actually costs you.
